messages.content: Write a polished short scene in modern American English focused on one adult character doing an ordinary task alone at home. Let the character's thoughts appear naturally through what they notice, remember, avoid, and do. Keep the internality specific and restrained rather than explaining everything. Use concrete details, varied sentence rhythm, and a clear sense of time passing. Avoid melodrama, generic filler, and broad statements about life.

Alex stood at the kitchen counter with a dish towel over one shoulder, staring at the same envelope she'd already opened twice.

The bill wasn't complicated. The amount was right there in the middle of the page, printed in numbers large enough to make pretending otherwise pointless.

She folded it along the existing crease.

Then unfolded it.

The washing machine kicked into its spin cycle in the next room. The floor gave a faint vibration under her bare feet.

Alex looked toward the hallway.

She could leave the envelope on the counter. She could deal with it tomorrow. Tomorrow was becoming an impressive category for things she didn't want to think about.

She opened the junk drawer and found three takeout menus, a dead pen, two batteries, and the little screwdriver she was always looking for.

The pen caught her attention.

She tested it on the back of the envelope.

Nothing.

“Of course,” she said to the empty kitchen.

She tossed it into the trash, then immediately reached in and pulled it back out.

The pen still didn't work.

“Right. Good talk.”

She dropped it in the drawer again.

The envelope remained on the counter.

Alex filled the kettle even though she hadn't decided whether she wanted tea. While it heated, she wiped down a clean patch of counter that didn't need wiping.

Her phone buzzed on the table.

She glanced at it.

A grocery reminder.

Milk. Eggs. Bread.

Ordinary things. Things that could be bought, carried home, put away.

She picked up her phone and added coffee to the list.

Then she looked back at the envelope.

“Tomorrow,” she said.

This time she slid it into the drawer instead of leaving it in the open.
